title: Real conversation
goal: Tell a friend what happened, react to their news, say which person or thing you mean, pass on what people said, and keep a chat going with the little words Pashtuns really use.
intro:
Most of the Pashto you'll speak isn't buying and asking the way — it's **ګپ شپ**: chatting over green tea, telling a friend what happened yesterday, reacting to their news, passing on what someone else said. This unit gives you the tools for that: words to tell events in order, reactions like **واه!**, **افسوس!** and **ټوکې کوې؟**, the all-purpose **چې** for 'the one who …', and the Pashto way of reporting speech.

As the last unit of Part 1, it pulls everything together — above all the past tense and its ergative construction, which you'll use every time you tell a friend what happened.

vocab.en: story; what happened, what's going on
vocab.note: f · pl: کيسې. کيسه کول 'to tell (what happened)'. کيسه څه ده؟ 'what's up?'
Present: پېښېږي peṣéẓi. Past: پېښ شو (m), پېښه شوه (f), پېښ شول (pl). Everyday speech also just uses کېدل: څه وشول؟

Literally 'after it'. In stories: لومړی … ورپسې … 'first … then …'.
همدا اوس 'right now, this minute'; همدا خبره ده 'that's exactly it'. همداسې 'just like that'.
Not for questions: کله؟ 'when?' but کله چې راغلم 'when I came'.
خبره داسې ده 'the thing is …'; داسې خلک 'people like that'.

phrases.roman: xabə́ra me pre kṛa, baṣə́na ġwā́ṛəm.

phrases.roman: ṣə no, wrústa ba xabə́re kawú.

grammar.title: Relative clauses with چې
grammar.body:
Pashto has no separate words for 'who', 'which', 'that' in relative clauses — it uses **چې** for all of them. The relative clause comes **after** the noun, starts with چې, and ends with its own verb:

هغه سړی **چې پرون راغی** زما تره دی
'The man **who came yesterday** is my uncle.'

The noun is often preceded by **هغه** 'that' or **دا** 'this', which signals that a relative clause is coming. The clause follows its own rules — so in the past it is ergative when *its* verb is transitive: هغه کتاب چې **ما** واخيست 'the book (that) I bought', هغه نجلۍ چې **مو** وليده 'the girl (that) we saw'. English often drops 'that'; Pashto never drops چې.

When the noun is the place or the person *in, to, with* which something happens, Pashto puts a small pronoun inside the clause where English has a preposition at the end: هغه هوټل چې **پکې** مو ډوډۍ وخوړه 'the restaurant we ate **in** (lit. in it)'.

With هر 'every' you get 'whatever / whoever': **هر څه چې** غواړې 'whatever you want', **هر څوک چې** راشي 'whoever comes'. And چې also means 'when' (کله چې), 'so that' (د دې لپاره چې) and, after verbs of saying and thinking, 'that'.

examples.native: هغه سړی چې پرون راغی زما تره دی.
examples.roman: haġá saṛáy che parún rā́ġay zmā trə day.
examples.en: The man who came yesterday is my uncle.

examples.native: هغه کتاب چې ما واخيست ډېر ښه دی.
examples.roman: haġá kitā́b che mā wā́xist ḍer ṣə day.
examples.en: The book I bought is very good.

examples.native: هغه نجلۍ چې په پوهنتون کې مو وليده د احمد خور ده.
examples.roman: haġá njlə́y che pə pohantún ke mo wə́lida də ahmád xor da.
examples.en: The girl we saw at the university is Ahmad's sister.

examples.native: هغه خبره چې تا راته وکړه رښتيا وه.
examples.roman: haġá xabə́ra che tā rā́ta wə́kṛa rəṣtyā́ wa.
examples.en: What you told me was true.

examples.native: کله چې کور ته ورسېدم، باران شروع شو.
examples.roman: kə́la che kor ta wə́rasedəm, bārā́n shurúʿ shu.
examples.en: When I got home, it started to rain.

grammar.title: Reported speech: keeping the original words
grammar.body:
Pashto normally reports speech **as it was said**, after **چې**, without changing pronouns or tenses the way English does:

هغه وويل چې **زه** ستړی **يم**
lit. 'He said that "I am tired"' = He said he was tired.

Only the context tells you that زه refers to 'him'. Questions are reported the same way: ما وپوښتل چې **ته** چېرته ځې؟ 'I asked where he was going' (lit. I asked: where are you going?).

Remember that **ويل** 'say' and **پوښتل** 'ask' are transitive, so in the past the speaker is oblique: **ما** وويل، **هغې** وپوښتل، **احمد** وويل. With no object, the verb takes the masculine plural form (وويل، وپوښتل). The same goes for 'who said?': **چا** وويل؟ — never څوک وويل.

To say who it was said *to*, use راته 'to me', درته 'to you', ورته 'to him / her / them' before the verb: ما **ورته** وويل چې … 'I told him that …'. A reported command keeps the imperative: راته يې وويل چې ژر راشه 'he told me to come quickly (lit. come quickly!)'.

**وايي چې** 'they say that' introduces rumours and hearsay: وايي چې سبا به باران وي.

examples.native: هغې وويل چې زه سبا نه شم راتلای.
examples.roman: haġé wə́wayəl che zə sabā́ na shəm rātlā́y.
examples.en: She said she couldn't come tomorrow.

examples.native: احمد وويل چې زه ډوډۍ نه غواړم.
examples.roman: ahmád wə́wayəl che zə ḍoḍə́y na ġwā́ṛəm.
examples.en: Ahmad said he didn't want any food.

examples.native: ما ترې وپوښتل چې ته د کوم ځای يې؟
examples.roman: mā tre wə́puṣtəl che tə də kum dzāy ye?
examples.en: I asked him where he was from.

examples.native: وايي چې دا لار خطرناکه ده.
examples.roman: wā́yi che dā lār xatarnā́ka da.
examples.en: They say this road is dangerous.

examples.native: مور مې راته وويل چې ژر کور ته راشه.
examples.roman: mor me rā́ta wə́wayəl che zhər kor ta rā́sha.
examples.en: My mother told me to come home soon.

grammar.title: Moving a story along — and sounding natural
grammar.body:
**Telling it in order:**
لومړی 'first' · بيا 'then' · ورپسې 'after that' · هغه وخت 'at that time' · ناڅاپه 'suddenly' · کله چې 'when' · خو 'but' · نو 'so' · په پای کې 'in the end'.

**Which past?** The **imperfective past** sets the scene — زه په سړک **تلم** 'I was going down the street', موږ ډوډۍ **خوړله** 'we were eating' — and the **perfective past** (with و-) moves the story forward: … ناڅاپه مې احمد **وليد** '… and suddenly I saw Ahmad'.

**The dramatic present.** At the exciting moment, friends switch to the present, just as English speakers do ('so I get home, and I look…'): کور ته ورسېدم، **ګورم** چې ټيلفون نشته! 'I got home, and I look — the phone's gone!'

**Fillers and reactions** that keep a chat going:
نو … 'so …' · يعنې 'I mean' · ګوره 'look' · مطلب دا چې 'the point is' · هو کنه 'yes, exactly' · ښه؟ 'right? OK?' · واه! 'wow!' · رښتيا؟ 'really?' · ټوکې کوې؟ 'are you kidding?' · افسوس! 'what a shame' · شاباس! 'well done!' · خير دی 'never mind' · هسې 'no reason, just'.

The trap: واه is only for good things. When a friend says their phone was stolen, it's **اوه!** or **افسوس!**

examples.native: زه په لار تلم، ناڅاپه مې يو زوړ ملګری وليد.
examples.roman: zə pə lār tləm, nātsā́pa me yaw zoṛ malgə́ray wə́lid.
examples.en: I was walking along the road when suddenly I saw an old friend.

examples.native: لومړی موږ چای وڅښه، بيا بازار ته ووتو.
examples.roman: lumṛáy muẓ chāy wə́tsṣə, biyā́ bāzā́r ta wə́watu.
examples.en: First we drank tea, then we went out to the bazaar.

examples.native: ورپسې احمد راغی، او بيا خو خندا شروع شوه!
examples.roman: warpáse ahmád rā́ġay, aw biyā́ xo xandā́ shurúʿ shwa!
examples.en: After that Ahmad turned up — and then the laughing really started!
So, you mean you're not going?

dialogue.title: The lost phone
dialogue.setting: Bilal runs into his friend Zalmay at a tea stall in Saddar, Peshawar.

lines.speaker: Bilal
lines.native: زلميه! کيسه څه ده؟ ډېر ستړی ښکارې.
lines.roman: zalmáya! kissá tsə da? ḍer stə́ṛay ṣkā́re.
lines.en: Zalmay! What's up? You look really tired.

lines.speaker: Zalmay
lines.native: ياره، مه يې پوښته! پرون مې ټيلفون ورک شو.
lines.roman: yā́ra, ma ye púṣta! parún me ṭelifún wrak shu.
lines.en: Man, don't ask! Yesterday I lost my phone.

lines.speaker: Zalmay
lines.native: په رکشه کې. کله چې کور ته ورسېدم، ګورم چې ټيلفون نشته!
lines.roman: pə rikshá ke. kə́la che kor ta wə́rasedəm, górəm che ṭelifún nə́shta!
lines.en: In a rickshaw. When I got home, I look — and the phone's gone!

lines.speaker: Zalmay
lines.native: ورور مې خپل ټيلفون راکړ، او ما خپلې شمېرې ته زنګ ووهه.
lines.roman: wror me xpəl ṭelifún rā́kaṛ, aw mā xpə́le shmeré ta zang wə́wahə.
lines.en: My brother gave me his phone, and I rang my own number.

lines.speaker: Zalmay
lines.native: يو سړي. هغه وويل چې زه د رکشې چلوونکی يم، ټيلفون دې زما سره دی.
lines.roman: yaw saṛí. haġə́ wə́wayəl che zə də rikshé chalawúnkay yəm, ṭelifún de zmā sara day.
lines.en: A man. He said he was the rickshaw driver and he had my phone.

lines.speaker: Zalmay
lines.native: نه ياره! نيم ساعت وروسته زموږ کور ته راغی، پيسې يې هم نه غوښتلې.
lines.roman: na yā́ra! nim sāʿát wrústa zmuẓ kor ta rā́ġay, páyse ye ham na ġuṣtə́le.
lines.en: No, man! Half an hour later he came to our house — and didn't even ask for money.

lines.speaker: Bilal
lines.native: شاباس! داسې خلک اوس ډېر کم دي.
lines.roman: shābā́s! dā́se xálək os ḍer kam di.
lines.en: Good for him! There aren't many people like that these days.

lines.speaker: Zalmay
lines.native: بالکل. ما ورته وويل چې ته ډېر ښه سړی يې.
lines.roman: bilkúl. mā wárta wə́wayəl che tə ḍer ṣə saṛáy ye.
lines.en: Exactly. I told him he was a really good man.

lines.speaker: Bilal
lines.native: ښه نو، اوس دې ټيلفون ښه وساته، لېونيه!
lines.roman: ṣə no, os de ṭelifún ṣə wə́sāta, lewanáya!
lines.en: Well then, look after your phone now, you nutter!

culture: Pashtun conversation is a team sport. Listeners keep the speaker going with **هو، هو**, **بيا؟** and **رښتيا؟**, and a good story is retold with voices, gestures and the dramatic present (**ګورم چې…** 'I look, and…'). Between friends of the same age, **ياره** and teasing like **لېونيه!** fly freely; with elders you switch to **تاسو**, call them **کاکا** 'uncle' or **حاجي صاحب**, and you don't interrupt. Chatting for hours over green tea — **ګپ شپ** — is the basic social activity, whether at a tea stall in Peshawar's Qissa Khwani, in a Kabul office or in a village حجره. Young people mix in English (OK, sorry, please, message), and in Pakistan Urdu words like **ويسې** 'by the way' and **بس** 'that's it'; Kabul Pashto speakers slip in Dari **بلې** 'yes' and **تشکر** 'thanks'. Swearing by God — **والله** (wallā́h) or **په خدای** — is the everyday way to say 'honestly!' and is not rude. **مبارک شه** — you've finished Part 1!

tip.title: ياره، کيسه څه ده؟ — opening a chat
tip.body:
- Between friends, call someone **ياره** 'mate, man' (the vocative of يار); to a woman friend use her name or **خورې**.
- **کيسه څه ده؟** 'what's the story?' = what's up, what's going on.
- Keep them talking with **او بيا؟** or **بيا څه وشول؟**
- ياره is only for friends your own age — with elders use **تاسو** and **صاحب**.
tip.pattern: ياره، کيسه څه ده؟  ·  او بيا؟

sentences.native: ياره، ولې خفه يې؟ څه پېښ شول؟
sentences.roman: yā́ra, wə́le xapá ye? tsə peṣ shwəl?
sentences.en: Man, why are you upset? What happened?

sentences.native: دا ډېره عجيبه کيسه ده.
sentences.roman: dā ḍéra ʿajíba kissá da.
sentences.en: That's a really weird story.

sentences.native: زما ملګري يوه عجيبه کيسه راته وکړه.
sentences.roman: zmā malgə́ri yáwa ʿajíba kissá rā́ta wə́kṛa.
sentences.en: My friend told me a strange story.

sentences.native: دا خو هره ورځ پېښېږي.
sentences.roman: dā xo hára wradz peṣéẓi.
sentences.en: But that happens every day.

sentences.native: ياره، دا عجيب سړی څوک دی؟
sentences.roman: yā́ra, dā ʿajíb saṛáy tsok day?
sentences.en: Mate, who's this weird guy?

sentences.native: او بيا؟ هغه څه وويل؟
sentences.roman: aw biyā́? haġə́ tsə wə́wayəl?
sentences.en: And then? What did he say?

sentences.native: ياره، کيسه دې ډېره اوږده ده!
sentences.roman: yā́ra, kissá de ḍéra úẓda da!
sentences.en: Man, your story is so long!

sentences.native: يار مې په کابل کې اوسېږي.
sentences.roman: yār me pə kābúl ke oséẓi.
sentences.en: My mate lives in Kabul.

sentences.native: دا عجيبه خبره ده، هغه هېڅکله ناوخته نه کېږي.
sentences.roman: dā ʿajíba xabə́ra da, haġá hetskə́la nāwáxta na kéẓi.
sentences.en: That's strange — he's never late.

sentences.native: بيا څه وشول؟ پوليس راغلل؟
sentences.roman: biyā́ tsə wə́shwəl? polís rā́ġləl?
sentences.en: Then what happened? Did the police come?

tip.title: First, then, suddenly: telling what happened
tip.body:
- Set the scene with the **imperfective past** (تلم 'I was going'); move the story on with the **perfective past** (ووتم 'I went out').
- Put it in order: **لومړی** first · **بيا** then · **ورپسې** after that · **ناڅاپه** suddenly · **کله چې** when · **په پای کې** in the end.
- At the exciting bit, friends switch to the present: ګورم چې… 'I look, and…'.

sentences.native: لومړی مو چای وڅښه، ورپسې ښار ته ووتو.
sentences.roman: lumṛáy mo chāy wə́tsṣə, warpáse ṣār ta wə́watu.
sentences.en: First we had tea, then we went out into town.

sentences.native: کله چې دفتر ته ورسېدم، دروازه بنده وه.
sentences.roman: kə́la che daftár ta wə́rasedəm, darwā́za bánda wa.
sentences.en: When I got to the office, the door was locked.

sentences.native: زه له کور نه ووتم او ناڅاپه باران شروع شو.
sentences.roman: zə la kor na wə́watəm aw nātsā́pa bārā́n shurúʿ shu.
sentences.en: I left the house and suddenly it started raining.

sentences.native: زه په سړک تلم، ګورم چې احمد راځي!
sentences.roman: zə pə saṛák tləm, górəm che ahmád rā́dzi!
sentences.en: I was walking down the street, and I look — there's Ahmad coming!

sentences.native: ګوره، همدا اوس له دفتر نه ووتم، ژر راځم.
sentences.roman: góra, hamdā́ os la daftár na wə́watəm, zhər rā́dzəm.
sentences.en: Look, I've just this minute left the office — I'll be there soon.

sentences.native: ورپسې ټول کور ته لاړل.
sentences.roman: warpáse ṭol kor ta lā́ṛəl.
sentences.en: After that everyone went home.

sentences.native: کله چې هغه راغی، موږ ډوډۍ خوړله.
sentences.roman: kə́la che haġá rā́ġay, muẓ ḍoḍə́y xwaṛə́la.
sentences.en: When he came, we were having dinner.

sentences.native: په پای کې موږ ټول ډېر وخندل.
sentences.roman: pə pāy ke muẓ ṭol ḍer wə́xandəl.
sentences.en: In the end we all had a good laugh.

sentences.native: خبره داسې وه چې زما ټيلفون ورک شو.
sentences.roman: xabə́ra dā́se wa che zmā ṭelifún wrak shu.
sentences.en: What happened was, my phone got lost.

tip.title: واه! افسوس! ټوکې کوې؟ — reacting like a friend
tip.body:
- Good news: **واه!** 'wow!' · **شاباس!** 'well done!'
- Bad news: **افسوس!** 'what a shame' or **اوه!** — never واه.
- Surprise: **رښتيا؟** 'really?' · **ټوکې کوې؟** 'are you kidding?'
- Agreeing: **بالکل** 'exactly' · **هو کنه!** 'yes, of course!' — and **بالکل نه** 'absolutely not'.

sentences.native: واه، نوی ټيلفون دې واخيست؟
sentences.roman: wāh, náway ṭelifún de wā́xist?
sentences.en: Wow, you bought a new phone?

sentences.native: شاباس! ډېر ښه کار دې وکړ.
sentences.roman: shābā́s! ḍer ṣə kār de wə́kaṛ.
sentences.en: Well done! You did a great job.

sentences.native: افسوس، نن نه شم راتلای.
sentences.roman: afsós, nən na shəm rātlā́y.
sentences.en: Shame — I can't come today.

sentences.native: افسوس! پلار دې لا ناروغ دی؟
sentences.roman: afsós! plār de lā nāróġ day?
sentences.en: Oh no! Is your father still ill?

sentences.native: ټوکې کوې؟ ته واده کوې؟
sentences.roman: ṭóke kawé? tə wādə́ kawé?
sentences.en: Are you kidding? You're getting married?

sentences.native: بالکل، ته سم وايې.
sentences.roman: bilkúl, tə sam wā́ye.
sentences.en: Absolutely, you're right.

sentences.native: بالکل نه! زه هېڅکله داسې نه کوم.
sentences.roman: bilkúl na! zə hetskə́la dā́se na kawə́m.
sentences.en: Absolutely not! I'd never do that.

sentences.native: ته لېونی يې؟ په دې يخني کې بهر ځې؟
sentences.roman: tə lewanáy ye? pə de yaxní ke bahár dze?
sentences.en: Are you crazy? You're going out in this cold?

sentences.native: واه! دا خو ډېر ښکلی کور دی.
sentences.roman: wāh! dā xo ḍer ṣkə́lay kor day.
sentences.en: Wow! What a lovely house.

tip.title: The man who…: چې after the noun
tip.body:
- The clause comes **after** the noun and starts with **چې**: هغه سړی **چې راغی** 'the man who came'.
- One چې does the work of who, which and that — never use څوک or کوم here.
- **هغه** or **دا** before the noun signals a clause is coming.
- In the past the clause keeps its own ergative: هغه کتاب چې **ما** واخيست 'the book I bought'.

sentences.native: هغه هلک چې له احمد سره دی زما ورور دی.
sentences.roman: haġá halə́k che la ahmád sara day zmā wror day.
sentences.en: The boy who's with Ahmad is my brother.

sentences.native: هغه ډوډۍ چې پرون مو وخوړه ډېره ګرانه وه.
sentences.roman: haġá ḍoḍə́y che parún mo wə́xwaṛa ḍéra grā́na wa.
sentences.en: The meal we had yesterday was really expensive.

sentences.native: هغه نجلۍ چې انګرېزي وايي د احمد خور ده.
sentences.roman: haġá njlə́y che angrezí wā́yi də ahmád xor da.
sentences.en: The girl who speaks English is Ahmad's sister.

sentences.native: هغه ټيلفون چې پرون مې واخيست ښه کار نه کوي.
sentences.roman: haġá ṭelifún che parún me wā́xist ṣə kār na kawí.
sentences.en: The phone I bought yesterday doesn't work properly.

sentences.native: ستا هغه ملګری چې په کابل کې اوسېږي څه کار کوي؟
sentences.roman: stā haġá malgə́ray che pə kābúl ke oséẓi tsə kār kawí?
sentences.en: What does that friend of yours who lives in Kabul do?

sentences.native: هغه سړی چې لکه ستا پلار ښکاري څوک دی؟
sentences.roman: haġá saṛáy che lə́ka stā plār ṣkā́ri tsok day?
sentences.en: Who's that man who looks like your father?

sentences.native: داسې ملګري چې تل مرسته کوي ډېر کم دي.
sentences.roman: dā́se malgə́ri che tal mrásta kawí ḍer kam di.
sentences.en: Friends who always help are hard to find.

sentences.native: يعنې څه؟ ته نه راځې؟
sentences.roman: yaʿné tsə? tə na rā́dze?
sentences.en: What do you mean? You're not coming?

sentences.native: زما مطلب دا و چې ته ستړی ښکارې.
sentences.roman: zmā matláb dā wə che tə stə́ṛay ṣkā́re.
sentences.en: What I meant was that you look tired.

tip.title: He said: «I'm tired» — reporting speech
tip.body:
- Report the words **as they were said**, after **چې**: هغه وويل چې **زه** ستړی **يم** 'he said he was tired'.
- Don't change 'I' to 'he' or shift the tense — the context does that.
- ويل 'say' and پوښتل 'ask' are transitive, so in the past the speaker is oblique: **ما** وويل، **هغې** وپوښتل، **چا** وويل؟
- **وايي چې…** = 'they say / apparently…'.
tip.pattern: ما / هغه / چا + وويل چې + the exact words

sentences.native: ما ورته وويل چې زه به سبا راشم.
sentences.roman: mā wárta wə́wayəl che zə ba sabā́ rā́shəm.
sentences.en: I told him I'd come tomorrow.

sentences.native: احمد وويل چې زه ناوخته کېږم.
sentences.roman: ahmád wə́wayəl che zə nāwáxta kéẓəm.
sentences.en: Ahmad said he's running late.

sentences.native: هغې وپوښتل چې ته چېرته اوسېږې؟
sentences.roman: haġé wə́puṣtəl che tə chérta oséẓe?
sentences.en: She asked where you live.

sentences.native: مور مې وويل چې ډوډۍ تياره ده.
sentences.roman: mor me wə́wayəl che ḍoḍə́y tayā́ra da.
sentences.en: My mum said the food is ready.

sentences.native: چا وويل چې زه واده کوم؟ دا دروغ دي!
sentences.roman: tsā wə́wayəl che zə wādə́ kawə́m? dā daróġ di!
sentences.en: Who said I'm getting married? That's a lie!

sentences.native: ما ترې وپوښتل چې ولې خفه يې؟ هغه وويل چې هسې.
sentences.roman: mā tre wə́puṣtəl che wə́le xapá ye? haġə́ wə́wayəl che háse.
sentences.en: I asked him why he was upset; he said "no reason".

sentences.native: ما اورېدلي چې هغه بهر ځي.
sentences.roman: mā awredə́li che haġá bahár dzi.
sentences.en: I've heard he's going abroad.

sentences.native: پوښتنه مې وکړه، خو ځواب يې رانه کړ.
sentences.roman: puṣtə́na me wə́kṛa, xo dzawā́b ye rā́na kaṛ.
sentences.en: I asked, but he didn't give me an answer.

sentences.native: هغه تل دروغ وايي.
sentences.roman: haġá tal daróġ wā́yi.
sentences.en: He always lies.

sentences.native: ګواکې هغه هېڅ نه پوهېږي!
sentences.roman: gwā́ke haġá hets na pohéẓi!
sentences.en: As if he doesn't know anything!

lessons.title: Chatting and joking
new: خبره مې پرې کړه، بښنه غواړم.
ښه نو، وروسته به خبرې کوو.

sentences.native: ټوکې مه کوه، رښتيا ووايه!
sentences.roman: ṭóke ma kawa, rəṣtyā́ wə́wāya!
sentences.en: Stop joking — tell me the truth!

sentences.native: هغه ډېرې ښې ټوکې کوي.
sentences.roman: haġá ḍére ṣe ṭóke kawí.
sentences.en: He tells really good jokes.

sentences.native: دا يوه ښه ټوکه وه!
sentences.roman: dā yáwa ṣa ṭóka wa!
sentences.en: That was a good joke!

sentences.native: له خندا مړ شوم!
sentences.roman: la xandā́ maṛ shwəm!
sentences.en: I died laughing!

sentences.native: ماښام به چای وڅښو او ګپ شپ به وکړو.
sentences.roman: māṣā́m ba chāy wə́tsṣu aw gap shap ba wə́kṛu.
sentences.en: In the evening we'll have tea and a chat.

sentences.native: غلی شه، ماشوم ويده دی.
sentences.roman: ġə́lay sha, māshúm widə́ day.
sentences.en: Be quiet, the baby is asleep.

sentences.native: ولې غلی يې؟ څه خبره ده؟
sentences.roman: wə́le ġə́lay ye? tsə xabə́ra da?
sentences.en: Why are you so quiet? What's the matter?

sentences.native: دا چای ستا لپاره دی.
sentences.roman: dā chāy stā lapā́ra day.
sentences.en: This tea is for you.

sentences.native: د ګپ شپ لپاره وخت نه لرم، بوخت يم.
sentences.roman: də gap shap lapā́ra waxt na lárəm, buxt yəm.
sentences.en: I don't have time for a chat, I'm busy.

sentences.native: بښنه غواړم، خبره مې پرې کړه. تا څه ويل؟
sentences.roman: baṣə́na ġwā́ṛəm, xabə́ra me pre kṛa. tā tsə wayə́l?
sentences.en: Sorry, I cut you off. What were you saying?

sentences.native: ښه نو، زه ځم، سبا به ګورو.
sentences.roman: ṣə no, zə dzəm, sabā́ ba góru.
sentences.en: OK then, I'm off — see you tomorrow.
